attributes.postTitle: Eoghan O'Connell named as October's Christophe Duchamp Player of the Month!

widgetData.content:
Eoghan O'Connell has been voted by County supporters as October's Christophe Duchamp Player of the Month winner, with the defender continuing to play a key role in the Hatters' promotion push.

The Irishman has quickly become an integral part of County's back-line since joining on a free transfer from Barnsley in the summer, starting all 14 of our league games this season under former teammate Jimmy McNulty.

Eoghan featured six times at the heart of County's back three during October and has flourished in a system that utilises his exceptional ball-playing abilities, with the defender often helping to initiate County's attacks from the back.

He helped County to four wins from those six games last month, keeping two clean sheets in the process, as the Hatters moved into the automatic promotion places heading into November.

It was also Eoghan's ball out from the back that led to Adama Sidibeh's crucial equaliser against Notts County at Meadow Lane, underlining the centre-half's contribution at both ends of the pitch.

New for this season, Player of the Month sponsor Christophe Duchamp will be providing a new watch to each of our winners, with Eoghan presented with this month's award after seeing off close competition from September's winner, Kyle Wootton.

County can move level on points with Huddersfield Town at the top of League One this weekend, as Jimmy McNulty’s side take on promotion rivals Reading at Edgeley Park.

The Hatters currently sit second in the table following a 2-1 win against AFC Wimbledon in their last league outing a fortnight ago. Goals from Jack Diamond and Ethan Ennis saw County come from behind to beat the Dons and secure a fourth consecutive home league win.

With leaders Huddersfield not in action this weekend due to the international break, a win would see County go level on points with the Terriers – although they would require a four-goal win to replace them at the top.

County have twice been in cup action since that win against Wimbledon, confirming top spot in their Jersey Mike’s Trophy group following a penalty shootout win against Tranmere Rovers, whilst also coming from 2-0 down with ten men to beat Cray Wanderers in the Emirates FA Cup. That incredible comeback win at Flamingo Park has set up a second round tie against this weekend’s opponents, Reading.

Leam Richardson’s side are also looking to narrow the gap at the top of the table this weekend following a strong start to the league season. The Royals currently sit four points behind County in sixth place, but were beaten 2-0 in their last league game away at rivals Oxford United.

A first win at Edgeley Park since 1971 would move them above Luton Town in the table and leave them a point behind County and the automatic promotion places.

Things you need to know:

  • The last remaining tickets for this game are available to purchase in the Cheadle End and the Pop Side! Click here to get tickets online today, and join us as we look for a fifth straight league win!
  • Please note that Edgeley Park is now a cashless stadium. Please ensure you have card or contactless payment methods ready for all purchases (excluding matchday bucket collections).
  • Don’t forget to turn up early to Edgeley Park to visit the County Courtyard! Doors open from 12pm. Click here for more details.
  • Saturday’s game will be available for overseas supporters to stream on County TV - featuring live commentary from Jon Keighren and Sam Byrne. Audio commentary will also be available for supporters based in the UK. Click here to subscribe to County TV.

Our Opponents:

Reading have endured a frustrating three seasons in the third tier since their relegation from the Championship in 2023. Prior to that year, the Royals hadn’t competed at this level since 2002, but they have failed to record a top six finish or challenge consistently for promotion since returning to League One.

They came close in 2024/25, missing out on the play-off places to Leyton Orient on the final day of the campaign despite a host of off-field issues. That impressive campaign provided plenty of optimism heading into last season under new ownership.

Three straight defeats to start the league campaign was not the start their supporters would have envisaged, however, and the Royals went on to win just two of their opening 12 league games to occupy a place in the relegation zone.

A much-needed victory was then secured against Northampton Town, but a 1-1 draw at home to Doncaster Rovers in their next league game saw the club part company with manager and club favourite, Noel Hunt.

Hunt had a popular five-year stint with the club during his playing days and came close to guiding them to an unlikely play-off spot in his first few months in charge, but departed with the club sitting 19th and just two points above the bottom four.

A swift recruitment process saw former Wigan Athletic and Rotherham United boss Leam Richardson appointed as Hunt’s successor. Richardson won the League One title with the Latics during his last spell in the third tier, but arrived on the back of overseeing Rotherham’s relegation from the Championship.

Richardson went unbeaten in his first three league games in charge, picking up wins against Stevenage and Blackpool in the process.

Consecutive defeats against Peterborough United and Bradford City left them still languishing down in 18th, but a superb run over the festive period soon saw them surge into the top half of the table.

The Royals won four and drew one of five league games between mid-December and January, a run capped by a 1-0 win against County at the Select Car Leasing Stadium.

Richardson’s side were just four points off the play-off places at that stage. Although they then suffered a brief dip in form, another strong run of just one defeat in nine saw them eventually break into the top six in March following a 2-1 win at Burton Albion.

They remained in the play-off places heading into April following a 3-0 win against Richardson’s former side, Wigan, but then went on to pick up just two points from their final six games, falling away to finish in 12th – 12 points behind Stevenage in sixth.

It was still an impressive turnaround from the situation that Richardson inherited back in October, and the manager was backed heavily in the transfer market over the summer.

Colchester United’s Kyreece Lisbie and former County loanee Josh Stokes have added further quality to a front line that already boasts one of the division’s best finishers in Jack Marriott.

It’s that exciting forward line that has shone in the opening months of the season, despite the Royals failing to win their opening two league games. A 4-3 defeat at home to Luton Town on the opening day was followed by a 0-0 draw with AFC Wimbledon, but a first win was then secured with a 5-0 thrashing of Mansfield Town.

Richardson picked up the League One Manager of the Month award for September after guiding Reading to further wins against Blackpool and Notts County, as well as picking up a point away at Wycombe.

They carried that momentum into October, with three wins and just one defeat in six league games moving them into the play-off places in League One. The highlight of that run was undoubtedly a 5-1 win away at MK Dons, with Lisbie grabbing a brace for the Royals.

The club’s razor-sharp attack has been blunted somewhat in their last two league games, drawing 0-0 at Plymouth Argyle before that 2-0 loss at Oxford, but they returned to form in some style in the Emirates FA Cup last weekend, winning 5-0 at Peterborough United.

Despite having to deal with a number of absentees this weekend through a combination of injury, suspension and international duty, they arrive at Edgeley Park in a good place – knowing a win will see them make further inroads at the top of the table.

Match Stats:

  • Saturday will be the 36th competitive meeting between the two sides. County have won ten of those previous encounters to Reading’s 12.
  • County have lost just two of 18 previous home games against Reading, going unbeaten in the last 13 meetings at Edgeley Park.
  • Kyle Wootton has scored in each of his two home appearances against Reading for County.

attributes.postTitle: Stockport County Community Trust to launch project for fans, supported by the Premier League

widgetData.content:
Stockport County Community Trust is delivering a fan-focused project with support from the Premier League Fans Fund. The Premier League Fans Fund provides grants to support football clubs at all levels of the game to strengthen connections between them, their fans, and local communities.

The fund supports a range of fan-focused and fan-led projects, helping to foster a sense of belonging through meaningful engagement. This includes schemes for under-represented groups, to further develop an inclusive and welcoming matchday experience for everyone.

 County Collective will use the reach and appeal of Stockport County to deliver targeted opportunities for engagement with key under represented communities across Stockport.  The project will support the development of a stronger sense of belonging between Stockport County Football Club, local communities and potential supporters who do not currently attend Edgeley Park.

Dan Landstrom, Head of Inclusion and Participation said: ‘“We’re excited to launch County Collective with support from the Premier League Fans Fund, building on our work with under-represented communities across Stockport.  Having a dedicated member of staff leading the project will help us reach more people who don’t currently attend Edgeley Park, create opportunities for them to get involved and build a stronger sense of belonging with Stockport County.

Open to professional football club charities in the Premier League, English Football League, Women’s Super League 1 and Women’s Super League 2, the Premier League Fans Fund builds on the Premier League and clubs’ commitment to ensuring long-term engagement with supporters. 

Following an initial £5million commitment in 2023-2025, the Premier League has committed a further £5million to the fund from 2026-2028. This will be administered through the Premier League Foundation.  During the fund’s first phase, more than 100 projects engaged over 18,000 participants through nearly 9,000 sessions.

Premier League Director of Community, Nick Perchard, said: “Fans are at the heart of football, and the strong connection between clubs and their supporters plays a vital role in the success of the game and the communities it serves.

“The Premier League Fans Fund is helping clubs strengthen those relationships by supporting projects that respond to the needs and interests of their fans. Through investment in initiatives at Premier League, EFL and WSL clubs across England and Wales, the Fund will help create more inclusive, engaging and meaningful opportunities for supporters, while delivering lasting benefits in communities and ensuring football remains a positive experience for all.”

 In season 2026/27, Premier League funding will support 137 fan-led projects that respond to local need, and which aim to improve the match day environment for fans, addressing a range of themes such as community cohesion; education, underrepresented fan groups and health and well-being.

Delivery is often themed around tackling inequalities to create community cohesion, covering areas like equality, diversity, and inclusion, mental health and wellbeing, physical health and wellbeing, providing education and training opportunities, supporting employability, and sustainability. 

Funding is flexible to empower professional football clubs, and their club charities, to develop fan-focused and fan-led projects that respond directly to the needs of their local community.

To find out more about the Premier League Fans Fund, please visit www.premierleague.com

attributes.postTitle: County proud to support Stroke Information this weekend

widgetData.content:
Supporters attending Saturday's fixture against Reading in Sky Bet League One will have the opportunity to support the charity Stroke Information, as volunteers collect donations around Edgeley Park ahead of kick-off and at half-time. 

Stroke Information was founded by Nick Clarke, a former Stockport County reserve-team player and steward, who now serves as the club's Disability Liaison and Access Officer. Following a severe stroke in 2012, Nick was determined to use his experience to help others facing similar challenges.

All of the charity's trustees have lived experience of stroke, with their guiding motto being: "We care because we've been there." Stroke Information provides vital support, advice and information to stroke survivors and their families, helping them navigate life after stroke and access the help available to them.

There are more than 7,300 stroke survivors living in Stockport alone, while over 17 million people worldwide experience a stroke every year. Through the charity's work, Nick hopes to help stroke survivors rebuild confidence, regain their sense of worth and ensure nobody feels they have to face their recovery journey alone.

Recent campaigns, including Survival Is Not Enough, have highlighted the ongoing challenges faced by stroke survivors and reinforced the importance of accessible support services within local communities.

Every contribution made this weekend will help Stroke Information continue to provide essential support to stroke survivors and their families across Stockport and beyond.

We would like to thank County supporters in advance for their generosity and encourage anyone attending the match to give what they can to support this fantastic local charity.

For more information about Stroke Information, visit www.strokeinformation.co.uk.

attributes.postTitle: Jersey Mike's Trophy Match Report: County 0-0 (4-3 pens.) Tranmere

widgetData.content:
The Hatters’ third and final group-stage match in the English Football League/Jersey Mike’s Trophy saw them make sure of finishing top of Northern Group E with a draw, followed by a victorious penalty shoot-out, at Edgeley Park against Tranmere.

With the Hatters having already qualified for the Second Round, the questions remaining were whether they would do so as table-toppers (with a view to being seeded for a home-tie next month), and if the League Two visitors, by avoiding defeat, could also go through to the knockout phase with one further game left to play.

As things turned out, both were achieved, as the fourth meeting between the two sides in the history of the competition ended scoreless - before a much-changed County team secured a bonus point to guarantee top spot in the group, as Luca Ashby-Hammond kept out two penalties, and Mamadou Jobe converted the fourth successful kick taken by the Hatters.

Shortly before the clock struck 7pm, the Hatters took to the field for an earlier-than-usual kick-off on a chilly, clear evening - and with a starting line-up showing nine changes from that in the FA Cup at Cray Wanderers two days earlier. The two survivors were Ashby-Hammond and Che Garner, whose minutes in the Cup-tie had been restricted to a little over 30 apiece due to the former’s dismissal and the latter’s consequential sacrifice for substitution. 

Eighteen-year-old central defender Dan Marshall, one of six teenagers handed a start, took his first-team bow for County - while the Hatters’ bench, like their initial 11, featured a good mix of further youth and more senior experience, including, in substitutes Lewis Bate, Ryan Glover and Jobe, three squad regulars who had not travelled to Cray. 

The Tranmere starters, meanwhile, included a couple of players boasting full international experience, with goalkeeper Coniah Boyce-Clarke and skipper Lee O’Connor having gained senior caps for Jamaica and the Republic of Ireland, respectively.

The visitors fashioned the tie’s first attempt in the third minute - courtesy of Olly Scott, who cut in from the right before stinging the hands of Ashby-Hammond. And, after another three, Ethan Ennis ran across the edge of the box to fire an inaugural shot for County for Boyce-Clarke to gather up.

Scott threatened again with just under a dozen minutes on the clock, after seizing upon a loose ball and advancing towards goal - only for his eventual shot to be blocked by Kyron Gordon, who was returning to match action for the first time in precisely one calendar month.

Ashby-Hammond dived to smother a low drive from the edge of the area by Charlie Veevers, and Richard Ilara put his foot in the way of Courtney Baker-Richardson’s goal-bound shot - before County, with three minutes of the first half remaining, went close with an Ennis shot and Bruno Cina’s follow-up that were respectively parried by Boyce-Clarke and blocked by David Kamara.

HALF-TIME: County 0, Tranmere 0. 

County made a quadruple-change upon the resumption - introducing Bate, Glover and Jobe, as well as Oliver Huddleston, who thereby made his senior debut, having missed out on doing so over the weekend whilst an unused substitute at Cray.

Tranmere brought on a pair of replacements shortly afterwards, and, just ahead of the hour, they combined to almost-decisive effect, with James Plant crossing from the right for Sam Mann - whose point-blank header was kept out by Ashby-Hammond.

With 17 minutes left on the clock, Plant sent over another delivery that Kamara - under pressure from Jobe - hooked high over the crossbar. And, three minutes later, Jobe was on hand again to block another close-range effort by Mann.

FULL-TIME: County 0, Tranmere 0. 

The penalties were taken at the Cheadle End, where Ashby-Hammond saved spot-kicks by Ryan Watson and Mann - as well as a third from Veevers, although that was wiped from the record and ordered to be re-taken - and, after Gardner's shot from 12 yards had been kept out, Jobe put away the decider, as the Hatters progressed to the knockout phase of the competition for the fourth successive season. 

PENALTIES: County 4 (Glover, Bailey, Huddleston, Jobe), Tranmere 3 (Nevett, Brough, Veevers).

Team (3-4-2-1): Ashby-Hammond; Gordon (Jobe, 46), Ilara (Maher, 67), Marshall; Osborn (Huddleston, 46), Bailey, Norwood (Capt.) (Bate, 46), Ennis (Glover, 46); C. Gardner, Astles; Cina. 

[Debuts for the following players, each with a unique SCAN [Stockport County Appearance Number]: Dan Marshall (1529); Oliver Huddleston (1530); and Jacob Maher (1531).]

Unused Subs: Jones, Singh.

Booked: Ilara.

Man of the Match: Marshall.

Attendance: 1,587 (225 away).

Reporter: Gareth Evans.

Photographer: Mike Petch.

attributes.postTitle: Match Report: York City Ladies 0-4 County Women

widgetData.content:
Stockport County Women climbed into third place in the FAWNL Division One North on Sunday with a thumping 4-0 win away at York City Ladies.

Tash Tezgel's side made it nine games unbeaten in all competitions with a dominant display on the road, leading after just seven minutes when Chloe Fisher fired home her first goal for the club. Imogen Porteous-Williams doubled the advantage before the break, with Katie Anderson and Porteous-Williams adding further goals in the second half to seal a resounding victory for the Hatters.

County made four changes to the side that beat Chesterfield in the FAWNL Cup the previous weekend, with Fisher coming in for her first league start for the club up front, following her summer move from Liverpool Feds.

Ruby Scott, Ellie Fletcher and Monika Stube also started for Tezgel's side, with Meg Parker, Maddie Robinson, Meg Boydell and Em Bradshaw dropping to the bench.

County were up and running in next to no time in Yorkshire, as Ellie Fletcher broke clear down the right flank in the seventh minute, with her ball in running through for Fisher to finish hard and low for her maiden Hatters goal.

York City almost responded immediately as Ella Martin fired an effort just over the crossbar, but then came a moment of controversy on 25 minutes as Ellie Fletcher broke clear of the York backline before being hauled down by a defender. Despite strong appeals for a red card from the travelling County supporters, the referee opted to show just a yellow.

It mattered little in any event for the Hatters, who doubled their lead just past the half-hour mark. Katie Anderson was the provider from midfield, sliding the ball through to Porteous-Williams, who beat the offside trap and fired home via the inside of the post for her sixth league goal of the campaign.

It could have been three for County before the break, with Fisher steering Fletcher's cut-back narrowly over the crossbar, but the Hatters went in at the break in a commanding position.

Half-Time: York City Ladies 0-2 County Women (Fisher, 7'; Porteous-Williams, 31').

The second half took a while to get going, although County remained in control throughout. Substitute Em Bradshaw then sparked the game into life on 67 minutes with a sensational solo run, taking on three York City players before seeing her effort well saved by goalkeeper Wallace.

The third goal came just a few minutes later, with Bradshaw releasing Livvi Turkington down the left, and her cross was headed home emphatically by Anderson for her second goal in as many games.

Three quickly became four for the Hatters, thanks to a moment of real quality from Porteous-Williams. Found in space 25 yards from goal, the forward looked up and hit a stunning effort into the top corner for her second of the game.

Yaz Ahmed was denied a fifth for County late on after seeing her back-post header well-saved, but County were still able to celebrate a third straight league success.

Momentum is gathering for Tash Tezgel's side, who climbed above Halifax and into the top three with Sunday's victory, sitting six points behind league leaders Leeds United.

For now, County's attention turns back to the Women's FA Cup, with the Hatters travelling to Boldmere St Michaels on Sunday 15th November for a second-round tie.

Full-Time: York City Ladies 0-4 County Women (Fisher, 7'; Porteous-Williams, 31' & 74'; Anderson, 71').

Wembley Play-Off Final 25/26 Programme

CLICK AND COLLECT FROM STOCKPORT COUNTY STORE

Wembley will be bathed in blue and white next Sunday as Stockport County descend on the national stadium for the League One Play-off Final, and supporters can reserve a commemorative copy of the EFL’s official matchday programme from the historic occasion.

Dave Challinor’s men eliminated Stevenage by a 3-0 aggregate scoreline in the semi-final to earn the right to face Bolton Wanderers in the showpiece finale and book a return visit to Wembley for the second time this campaign.

County, who finished third in the League One table for the second successive season, are seeking to end a 24-year absence from the Championship with victory against their Greater Manchester neighbours in the capital.

With exclusive interviews from Louie Barry and Ben Osborn, as well as a welcome from the boss, the 100-page A4 commemorative publication provides the perfect keepsake from this grandest of occasions playing out on the Wembley turf.

The matchday programme from the EFL’s official publication partners, Ignition Sports Media, can be purchased from sellers around Wembley on matchday or can be pre-ordered now.

These official matchday souvenirs are priced at £10 each, plus post and packaging to a UK address, and will aim to be posted via Royal Mail on Friday 22nd May if pre-ordered before Thursday 21st May.

Bergara Gin by Stockport Gin
products.body_html:
Bergara Gin was originally launched by us at Stockport Gin to raise money for the Danny Bergara statue at Edgeley Park.

The initial release raised over £3000 for the fund and the gin was incredibly popular, so much so that people have always asked us to bring it back. However, we didn't want to bring it back without another purpose - and now we have found it! Bergara Gin is back in collaboration with the Stockport County Community Trust and 20% of every bottle we sell will be donated to the Kits by County fund.

The gin itself is inspired by Danny Bergara and his Uruguayan heritage. It is distilled here at Stockport Gin at our distillery in Stockport Town Centre with yellow passion fruit and feijoa, tropical fruits native to Uruguay, alongside Yerba Mate, a traditional Uruguayan herbal tea.

Bergara Gin relaunches on Saturday 29th November at 3pm at www.stockport-gin.com/bergaragin - or, if you want to be one of the first to get your hands on a bottle, a limited number of bottles will be available in the Club Shop after the game on Saturday!
